caption: The video captures an overhead close view of a pour-over setup, with a mint-green cone dripper lined by a white fluted filter holding a bed of blooming, foam-topped grounds on a black digital scale atop dark wood. A thin stream of water falls continuously from a metallic gooseneck kettle whose curved spout enters from the right. A hand wearing a ring grips the handle at the bottom left, steering the pour. The stream's landing point shifts only slightly near the center, keeping a dark crater in the foam while surface bubbles churn and pop. The liquid level in the filter rises gradually as more water is added, and the scale's weight reading increases in irregular jumps while the timer advances. The framing and background wood grain remain fixed.
relations: Continuous water stream from the kettle causes the foam surface to churn and pop as the landing point shifts.
Adding water raises the liquid level in the filter while the scale's weight reading increases in irregular jumps.
The hand steering the kettle adjusts the stream slightly, maintaining a dark crater in the blooming grounds.
As the timer advances, the pour continues, keeping the foam agitated and the liquid level rising.
